segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have an advanced level lesson for you. This one's a bit difficult.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为您准备了高级课程。 这个有点难。

segments.en: It's all about science.
segments.zh: 这一切都与科学有关。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we're going to talk about physics, specifically about, well you know, things like Stephen Hawking and wormholes, black holes and general theory of relativity and all that good stuff.
segments.zh: 今天我们将讨论物理学，特别是关于斯蒂芬霍金和虫洞、黑洞和广义相对论的东西，以及所有这些好东西。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So we're in class.
segments.zh: 所以我们在上课。

segments.en: We're learning about physics today and you're going to hear a lot of terms.
segments.zh: 我们今天正在学习物理学，你会听到很多术语。

segments.en: Don't worry if you're not really sure what they mean.
segments.zh: 如果您不确定它们的含义，请不要担心。

segments.en: We'll be back in a moment to talk about them.
segments.zh: 我们稍后会回来谈论他们。

segments.en: Good morning, everybody. Welcome to Physics 101.
segments.zh: 大家早上好，欢迎来到物理学入门课。

segments.en: My name is Ed Brown and I will be your professor for the semester.
segments.zh: 我的名字是 Ed Brown，我将成为你这个学期的教授。

segments.en: Since today is our first day, I wanted to give you an overview of what this course will look like, how you will be graded and what we will cover this semester.
segments.zh: 今天是第一堂课，我想先介绍一下课程安排、评分方式，以及本学期要学的内容。

segments.en: Will we be focusing more on theoretical physics or experimental physics, professor?
segments.zh: 教授，我们会更多地关注理论物理或实验物理吗？

segments.en: This is an introductory course and my aim is to give you a broad overview of the field of physics.
segments.zh: 这是一门入门课程，我的目的是为您提供物理学领域的广泛概述。

segments.en: The term physics encompasses many different areas of research and study.
segments.zh: 物理学一词包含许多不同的研究和研究领域。

segments.en: And I hope this course will provide you with a conceptual understanding of physics, which will prove useful whether or not you choose to further your study in the field.
segments.zh: 我希望这门课程能为您提供对物理学的概念理解，无论您是否选择在该领域继续学习，这将证明是有用的。

segments.en: We will begin the course by looking at the fundamental concepts of physics.
segments.zh: 我们将从物理学的基本概念开始课程。

segments.en: Then by the middle of the semester, we will begin exploring the more theoretical side of physics.
segments.zh: 然后到学期中期，我们将开始探索物理学更理论的一面。

segments.en: It is essential that you first have a firm grasp of the fundamentals so that you can better understand the theoretical concepts when we get to them.
segments.zh: 你们必须先牢牢掌握基础知识，这样之后学到理论概念时，才能更好地理解。

segments.en: Will we learn about black holes, wormholes and string theory?
segments.zh: 我们会了解黑洞、虫洞和弦理论吗？

segments.en: We will learn about the general theory of relativity, including black holes.
segments.zh: 我们将了解广义相对论，包括黑洞。

segments.en: We will also explore the developing theories in quantum mechanics, such as string theory.
segments.zh: 我们还将探索量子力学中的发展理论，例如弦理论。

segments.en: We will discuss some hypothetical features of space-time, like wormholes.
segments.zh: 我们将讨论时空的一些假设特征，例如虫洞。

segments.en: We will also explore some of the more influential developments in the field of thermodynamics, electromagnetism and nuclear physics, all of which have had significant impacts on modern life.
segments.zh: 我们还将探索热力学、电磁学和核物理学领域中一些更有影响力的发展，所有这些对现代生活都产生了重大影响。

segments.en: Now I am going to have the TAs pass out the syllabus for this class, so you can see how this course will be graded.
segments.zh: 现在我请助教把课程大纲发下去，大家可以看看这门课的评分方式。

segments.en: Oh man, looks like this isn't going to be the easy A I thought it would be.
segments.zh: 唉，看来这门课不像我想的那样，能轻轻松松拿个 A 了。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So obviously we are in a class, as you said, and the professor is pretty much introducing the course and what's going to happen during the semester.
segments.zh: 所以显然我们在上课，正如你所说，教授几乎是在介绍这门课程以及学期将要发生的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So he's talking about the different kinds of physics or the different elements of physics that will be a part of this course.
segments.zh: 所以他正在谈论将成为本课程一部分的不同类型的物理学或不同的物理元素。

segments.en: And there's a very eager student, he's very excited and he wants to know, are these interesting things going to be a part of the course?
segments.zh: 有一个非常渴望的学生，他非常兴奋，他想知道，这些有趣的事情会成为课程的一部分吗？

segments.en: And so when we start out, we talked about these two different fields of physics and I think maybe it would be helpful to start there with these two branches of this field.
segments.zh: 所以当我们开始时，我们讨论了这两个不同的物理学领域，我认为从这个领域的这两个分支开始可能会有所帮助。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: He mentioned, this boy Matt said, if they're going to be focusing more on theoretical physics or experimental physics.
segments.zh: 他提到，这个男孩马特说，如果他们要更多地关注理论物理学或实验物理学。

segments.en: Now, theoretical physics and experimental physics are what we call two different branches of physics.
segments.zh: 现在，理论物理学和实验物理学是我们所说的物理学的两个不同分支。

segments.en: That means they're both physics.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们都是物理学。

segments.en: But people who do them have different methods and maybe focus on different things.
segments.zh: 但是做这些的人有不同的方法，可能专注于不同的事情。

segments.en: Theoretical comes from the word theory.
segments.zh: 理论来自理论。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So I have a theory about something and I'm going to think about whether or not it's possible and maybe there's some math involved.
segments.zh: 所以我有一个关于某事的理论，我会考虑是否可能，并且可能涉及一些数学。

segments.en: But with experimental physics, the key word here is experiment, experimental.
segments.zh: 但对于实验物理学，这里的关键词是实验、实验。

segments.en: That means we actually build experiments to test our theories.
segments.zh: 这意味着我们实际上建立了实验来测试我们的理论。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So I guess theoretical physics, we can just have theories about how things happen or explain them, but we can't really prove them.
segments.zh: 所以我猜理论物理学，我们可以有关于事情如何发生或解释的理论，但我们无法真正证明它们。

segments.en: We can just have theories around them.
segments.zh: 我们可以围绕它们进行理论。

segments.en: Maybe we can try and prove them mathematically.
segments.zh: 也许我们可以尝试在数学上证明它们。

segments.en: But experimental physics, you can actually, as you said, create an experiment to prove it or not.
segments.zh: 但是实验物理学，正如你所说，你可以创建一个实验来证明这一点。

segments.en: That's right. And so those are the two main branches that the young man asks about.
segments.zh: 没错。 这就是年轻人问的两个主要分支。

segments.en: But the professor says, you know, listen, we're going to be talking about the fundamental concepts of physics.
segments.zh: 但教授说，你知道，听着，我们将谈论物理学的基本概念。

segments.en: And so fundamental concepts are things that you often hear a professor talk about in your introductory class.
segments.zh: 因此，基本概念是您在介绍性课程中经常听到教授谈论的事情。

segments.en: So introduction to mathematics or introduction to physics.
segments.zh: 所以数学导论或物理学导论。

segments.en: So fundamental concepts are the basics.
segments.zh: 所以基本概念是基础。

segments.en: That's right. So the most important, but also the ones at the very bottom, the foundation.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以最重要的，也是最底层的基础。

segments.en: Because you can learn about more difficult or more complicated things later.
segments.zh: 因为您以后可以了解更困难或更复杂的事情。

segments.en: But first, you have to have a foundation. So those are the fundamental concepts.
segments.zh: 但首先，你必须有一个基础。 所以这些是基本概念。

segments.en: Right. And actually, after the professor said that, this other, this guy, Matt, went on to ask if they were going to learn about black holes, wormholes and string theory.
segments.zh: 对。 实际上，在教授说之后，另一个人，马特，继续询问他们是否要了解黑洞、虫洞和弦理论。

segments.en: OK, so three very important parts of physics, but very, very complicated things.
segments.zh: 好的，所以物理学的三个非常重要的部分，但非常非常复杂的事情。

segments.en: The first two are related, right? So we've got astrophysics.
segments.zh: 前两个是相关的，对吧？ 所以我们有天体物理学。

segments.en: Astro means star. So astrophysics is the physics of things, bodies in space, planets, stars, things like that.
segments.zh: 太空人的意思是星星。 所以天体物理学是事物的物理学，太空中的物体，行星，恒星，类似的东西。

segments.en: That's right. And so two concepts that we often talk about in astrophysics are black holes and wormholes.
segments.zh: 没错。 因此，我们在天体物理学中经常谈论的两个概念是黑洞和虫洞。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So I think many of you have already heard this word, black hole.
segments.zh: 所以我想你们中的许多人已经听说过这个词，黑洞。

segments.en: The concept of it is basically a huge hole in space that just sucks up everything.
segments.zh: 它的概念基本上是一个巨大的太空洞，它只会吸收一切。

segments.en: The gravitational force. So the pull of gravity is so strong that nothing can resist it.
segments.zh: 引力。 所以重力的拉力是如此强烈，以至于没有什么能抵抗它。

segments.en: Everything that comes close to a black hole, it's like in a drain.
segments.zh: 靠近黑洞的一切，就像在排水沟里一样。

segments.en: Everything that comes close to it gets sucked in. No light can escape it.
segments.zh: 接近它的一切都被吸进去。没有光可以逃脱它。

segments.en: That's right. And the other concept there is a wormhole.
segments.zh: 没错。 另一个概念有一个虫洞。

segments.en: So it's basically a sort of bending of space and time in which you can travel from one point to another a lot faster than going in a straight line.
segments.zh: 所以它基本上是一种空间和时间的弯曲，你可以从一个点到另一个点比直线快得多。

segments.en: Or from one time to another.
segments.zh: 或从一次到另一次。

segments.en: So this is a very, very popular concept in science fiction movies and books.
segments.zh: 所以这是科幻电影和书籍中非常非常流行的概念。

segments.en: For example, Star Trek, the most recent movie, the new movie Star Trek, there was a wormhole.
segments.zh: 例如，最近的电影《星际迷航》，新电影《星际迷航》，有一个虫洞。

segments.en: So one ship goes from the future and it comes into the past.
segments.zh: 所以一艘船从未来开始，它会进入过去。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it has to travel through this wormhole.
segments.zh: 所以它必须穿过这个虫洞。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And actually, yeah, you say science fiction and obviously it's hard to prove it, but this is one of the concepts that physicists think they can prove someday.
segments.zh: 实际上，是的，你说的是科幻小说，显然很难证明这一点，但这是物理学家认为他们有一天可以证明的概念之一。

segments.en: Someday.
segments.zh: 总有一天。

segments.en: And this is why it's a part of theoretical physics.
segments.zh: 这就是为什么它是理论物理学的一部分。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And what about this other concept, string theory?
segments.zh: 那么另一个概念，弦理论呢？

segments.en: Okay, string theory is a theory about the way the world works, basically.
segments.zh: 好吧，弦理论基本上是关于世界运作方式的理论。

segments.en: And it is a theory that actually competes with Einstein's view of the way the world works, right?
segments.zh: 它是一个真正与爱因斯坦对世界运作方式的观点竞争的理论，对吧？

segments.en: And string theory is about basically strings that are vibrating and that's the way the entire universe is kind of built.
segments.zh: 弦理论基本上是关于振动的字符串，这就是整个宇宙的构建方式。

segments.en: Yeah, so basically at the subatomic level, usually you're supposed to have an atom, but also supposedly these atoms are made up of strings that depending on the frequency at which they vibrate, they can constitute different elements or different parts.
segments.zh: 是的，所以基本上在亚原子水平上，通常你应该有一个原子，但也可以说这些原子是由弦组成的，取决于它们振动的频率，它们可以构成不同的元素或不同的部分。

segments.en: Different kinds of matter, right.
segments.zh: 不同的物质，对。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And so we're talking about the very, very, very, very, very, very, very smallest building blocks of the things in the world, atoms and even quarks and joules and those things.
segments.zh: 所以我们谈论的是世界上事物的非常、非常、非常、非常、非常、非常小的组成部分，原子甚至夸克和焦耳以及那些东西。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So it's actually one of these new things that, well, people are talking about string theory.
segments.zh: 所以它实际上是这些新事物之一，人们正在谈论弦理论。

segments.en: It's kind of this new way of seeing the world and explaining the unexplainable because there are so many things still in the world that we can't explain.
segments.zh: 这是一种看待世界和解释无法解释的新方式，因为世界上还有很多事情我们无法解释。

segments.en: And people argue about this because obviously if you can't prove it, it's hard to say what is right and what is wrong.
segments.zh: 人们争论这一点，因为显然如果你不能证明这一点，就很难说什么是对的，什么是错的。

segments.en: Exactly. But actually one thing that was proven was Einstein's general theory of relativity.
segments.zh: 没错。 但实际上被证明的一件事是爱因斯坦的广义相对论。

segments.en: So this is something we all learned back in high school or in college.
segments.zh: 所以这是我们在高中或大学时都学到的东西。

segments.en: That's right. So basically the general theory of relativity is this idea that space and time are not fixed.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以基本上相对论的一般理论是空间和时间不是固定的。

segments.en: They're relative to each other.
segments.zh: 它们是相对的。

segments.en: So an example my teacher used to use is that when you travel very, very, very fast, imagine going around a jet around the world counterclockwise, time slows down the faster you move.
segments.zh: 所以我的老师过去常用的一个例子是，当你非常、非常、非常快地旅行时，想象一下逆时针绕着世界的喷气式飞机，你移动的速度越快，时间就会变慢。

segments.en: Okay, so that proves that time and space are not fixed.
segments.zh: 好吧，这证明了时间和空间不是固定的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Actually, the general theory of relativity and specifically this aspect of speed and time was proven with the example that you give with two atomic clocks.
segments.zh: 实际上，相对论的一般理论，特别是速度和时间的这一方面，你用两个原子钟给出的例子得到了证明。

segments.en: You kept one on the ground, like, I don't know, in your house, and you put one in an airplane that was traveling faster than the speed of sound.
segments.zh: 你把一个放在地上，就像，我不知道，在你的房子里，你把一架放在一架比音速快的飞机上。

segments.en: And so after maybe an hour, the plane would land and the clocks would have not the same time anymore, but they would be one, the clock that was in the airplane traveling faster would be maybe half a second off or something very, very small.
segments.zh: 因此，大概一个小时后，飞机将降落，时钟将不再是同一时间，但它们将是一个，飞机上的时钟可能会偏离半秒或非常非常小的时间。

segments.en: But you would see that time moves slower because your speed is faster.
segments.zh: 但是你会看到时间移动得更慢，因为你的速度更快。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's the general theory.
segments.zh: 这就是一般理论。

segments.en: That's a part of the general theory of relativity.
segments.zh: 这是广义相对论的一部分。

segments.en: It's a very important theory in the history of the world, but also in the history of physics.
segments.zh: 它是世界历史上非常重要的理论，也是物理史上的一个非常重要的理论。

segments.en: Another thing, though, that the professor mentioned that is very important in physics these days is quantum mechanics.
segments.zh: 然而，教授提到的另一件事，如今在物理学中非常重要的是量子力学。

segments.en: Yes, this is actually a very interesting field of physics, but very hard to understand.
segments.zh: 是的，这实际上是一个非常有趣的物理学领域，但很难理解。

segments.en: In my opinion, for me, it's very, very hard.
segments.zh: 在我看来，对我来说，这非常非常困难。

segments.en: I find it very complex, too. Well, mechanics are the way things work, right?
segments.zh: 我也觉得很复杂。 好吧，机械师是事情的运作方式，对吧？

segments.en: And so quantum is at the atomic and subatomic level.
segments.zh: 因此，量子处于原子和亚原子水平。

segments.en: And so you're talking about basically the building blocks of the things in the universe.
segments.zh: 所以你说的基本上是宇宙中事物的基石。

segments.en: And the people who are studying this or working on this, quantum mechanics, they don't like the Einsteinians.
segments.zh: 而那些研究这个或研究这个的人，量子力学，他们不喜欢爱因斯坦人。

segments.en: They don't like the people who follow Einstein because these two theories, they don't actually go together very well.
segments.zh: 他们不喜欢追随爱因斯坦的人，因为这两种理论，他们实际上并没有很好地结合在一起。

segments.en: You either have to believe one or you have to believe the other.
segments.zh: 你要么必须相信一种，要么你必须相信另一个。

segments.en: Well, the problem is that when you're talking at the macro level, the way things work and the way things move, like for example, you and me, of course, there are formulas and there are everything that explains and that proves that things are the way they are.
segments.zh: 好吧，问题在于，当你在宏观层面上讲话时，事物的运作方式和事物的移动方式，例如，你和我，当然，有公式和一切都可以解释，这证明事情就是这样。

segments.en: But the problem is that in quantum mechanics at the subatomic level, it's so different.
segments.zh: 但问题在于，在亚原子级的量子力学中，它是如此不同。

segments.en: Like, for example, electronics, the reason why we're able to have microprocessors and electronics is because, for example, atoms can be in two places at the same time, which is impossible in our world.
segments.zh: 例如，电子产品，我们能够拥有微处理器和电子产品的原因是，例如，原子可以同时在两个地方，这在我们的世界中是不可能的。

segments.en: It's like saying, you know, Catherine can be in two places at the exact same time.
segments.zh: 这就像说，你知道，凯瑟琳可以同时在两个地方。

segments.en: And there's also this problem of observation that I've read about.
segments.zh: 还有我读过的这个观察问题。

segments.en: So there are some kinds of particles like electrons, for example, that if you're observing them, sometimes appear as waves.
segments.zh: 所以有一些像电子这样的粒子，例如，如果你观察它们，有时会表现为波。

segments.en: But if you're observing them, sometimes appear to have mass.
segments.zh: 但如果你在观察它们，有时似乎有质量。

segments.en: Exactly like light.
segments.zh: 就像光一样。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you're talking about these things that seem to have a whole different set of rules from the rules that we have here walking around and eating food and going to work.
segments.zh: 所以你说的是这些似乎与我们在这里走来走去、吃食物和工作的规则完全不同的规则。

segments.en: And so I think that's what's fascinating about physics, that, you know, you can break things down to the very smallest parts and they seem very different.
segments.zh: 所以我认为这就是物理学的迷人之处，你知道，你可以把事情分解成最小的部分，而且它们看起来非常不同。

segments.en: Or you can think about the stars and the moon and, you know, these planets and they have their own rules, too.
segments.zh: 或者你可以想想星星和月球，你知道，这些行星也有自己的规则。

segments.en: And so, you know, that's why physics is such a very, I think it's, it's, it's frustrating.
segments.zh: 所以，你知道，这就是为什么物理学如此，我认为它是，它，它令人沮丧。

segments.en: It's frustrating and it's exciting at the same time.
segments.zh: 这令人沮丧，同时令人兴奋。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And actually some of the other fields that the professor said they were going to explore are the fields of thermodynamics, electromagnetism and even nuclear physics.
segments.zh: 实际上，教授说他们将要探索的其他一些领域是热力学、电磁学甚至核物理学领域。

segments.en: So very important branches, I think, of physics as well.
segments.zh: 我认为，非常重要的分支也是物理学。

segments.en: So when you're studying physics or science, you will definitely hear about the laws of thermodynamics.
segments.zh: 因此，当您学习物理或科学时，您肯定会听到热力学定律。

segments.en: Thermo means heat and dynamics means, you know, changing, changing state.
segments.zh: 热意味着热量，动力学意味着，你知道，改变，改变状态。

segments.en: And electromagnetism, of course, is the combination of two words, electricity and magnetism.
segments.zh: 当然，电磁学是两个词的组合，电和磁。

segments.en: You know, like magnets, you have the plus end and the minus end.
segments.zh: 你知道，就像磁铁一样，你有加末端和负端。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: They attract or they repel.
segments.zh: 它们吸引或排斥。

segments.en: Then finally, nuclear physics.
segments.zh: 最后，核物理。

segments.en: Nuclear physics is very important because it's, again, about the, about atoms and breaking down atoms and finding out what their parts are.
segments.zh: 核物理学非常重要，因为它同样是关于原子和分解原子并找出它们的部分是什么。

segments.en: So you might have heard about the Hadron Super Collider.
segments.zh: 所以你可能听说过强子超级对撞机。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: This is like a big, it's like a big racetrack for atoms and they basically spin these atoms around the racetrack going faster and faster.
segments.zh: 这就像一个大的，它就像一个大型的原子赛道，它们基本上在赛道上旋转这些原子越来越快。

segments.en: And then they put objects in their way so that they break.
segments.zh: 然后他们把物体挡在他们的路上，这样它们就破裂了。

segments.en: They crash.
segments.zh: 他们崩溃了。

segments.en: They crash.
segments.zh: 他们崩溃了。

segments.en: And they study what the pieces look like.
segments.zh: 他们研究这些作品的样子。

segments.en: And what happens and how much energy is released.
segments.zh: 以及发生了什么以及释放了多少能量。

segments.en: It's all very interesting and it seems like things that are out of science fiction because it's not something mainstream that you hear about in the news very often.
segments.zh: 这一切都很有趣，而且似乎是科幻小说中的东西，因为它不是你经常在新闻中听到的主流的东西。

segments.en: Or that sometimes we understand, like obviously we all hear about the gossip magazines and who's dating who and all this other type of news.
segments.zh: 或者有时我们理解，就像我们都听说过八卦杂志和谁在和谁和所有其他类型的新闻约会一样。

segments.en: But very rarely do we really pay attention to this type of information or news because it is a little bit complex to understand.
segments.zh: 但我们很少真正关注这种类型的信息或新闻，因为它有点难以理解。

segments.en: And it seems that, I think scientists are not the best writers for average people like you and me.
segments.zh: 似乎，我认为科学家并不是像你我这样的普通人的最佳作家。

segments.en: They write in their own language almost.
segments.zh: 他们几乎用自己的语言写作。

segments.en: Oftentimes that's the case.
segments.zh: 通常情况就是这样。

segments.en: But I have to say I recently read Bill Bryson's book, A Short History of Nearly Everything, and it talks about the history of the world and us and the animals and plants in it.
segments.zh: 但我不得不说我最近读了比尔·布莱森的书《几乎所有事物的简短历史》，它讲述了世界的历史以及我们以及其中的动植物。

segments.en: And he talks about physics especially.
segments.zh: 他尤其谈到物理学。

segments.en: And I think that if you're interested in that, I don't know, I mean if you're an advanced English learner, it might be challenging.
segments.zh: 我认为如果你对此感兴趣，我不知道，我的意思是如果你是一名高级英语学习者，那可能会很有挑战性。

segments.en: It was challenging for me.
segments.zh: 这对我来说很有挑战性。

segments.en: But it's definitely a good book to read to learn about some of these things.
segments.zh: 但它绝对是一本很好的书来了解其中的一些东西。

segments.en: Yeah, it's actually a very good idea.
segments.zh: 是的，这实际上是一个非常好的主意。

segments.en: And I don't know, many of us, I think many of us as well growing up, maybe we had a hard time with some of these exact sciences like chemistry or physics.
segments.zh: 而且我不知道，我们中的许多人，我认为我们中的许多人都长大了，也许我们很难使用一些精确的科学，如化学或物理。

segments.en: So we obviously find it hard to be interested in it.
segments.zh: 所以我们显然很难对它感兴趣。

segments.en: But you know it's very different because it's not math and formulas.
segments.zh: 但你知道它非常不同，因为它不是数学和公式。

segments.en: You don't really have to know how to derive the formula or anything.
segments.zh: 你真的不必知道如何推导出公式或任何东西。

segments.en: You just kind of have to understand the theory.
segments.zh: 你只需要理解这个理论。

segments.en: And it's very, very interesting I must say.
segments.zh: 我必须说，这非常非常有趣。

segments.en: It is and it's fun because you can talk about, it's like philosophy sometimes, you can talk about if this were the case, then what would happen.
segments.zh: 它很有趣，因为你可以谈论，它就像哲学有时，你可以谈论如果是这样，那么会发生什么。

segments.en: These hypothetical situations and I think that's maybe more in line with theoretical physics.
segments.zh: 这些假设的情况，我认为这可能更符合理论物理学。

segments.en: But it's really interesting to think about and to let your mind go into these very strange places.
segments.zh: 但思考并让你的思想进入这些非常奇怪的地方真的很有趣。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So actually we are curious to know if you believe that maybe someday we will be able to travel in time.
segments.zh: 所以实际上我们很想知道你是否相信有一天我们可以及时旅行。

segments.en: Or do you believe that… Live on other planets or we'll have space travel as a part of our holiday making.
segments.zh: 或者你相信……住在其他星球上，否则我们将把太空旅行作为我们假期制作的一部分。

segments.en: Yeah, they supposedly already are arranging tourism to the moon, right?
segments.zh: 是的，他们应该已经在安排旅游到月球，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, they are.
segments.zh: 是的，他们是。

segments.en: So I wonder if one day like in the fifth element we're going to have these cruises to space.
segments.zh: 所以我想知道有一天，我们是否会像在第五个元素中那样让这些游轮飞往太空。

segments.en: Yeah, that would be fun.
segments.zh: 是的，那会很有趣。

segments.zh: 我们希望在那里见到你，直到下一次。

segments.zh: 再见。
